record.tranche_reason: Tests whether fine-tuning on a subset of forgotten data restores WMDP-Bio performance, using a relearning evaluation on unlearned checkpoints.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports unlearning benchmark results, but those do not test recovery under an attack and are not included as rows. Its discussion of reversibility and other cited studies is background, not this study's result.
record.test_reason: Runs a relearning attack (fine-tune on 20% of the WMDP-Bio forget set, 1000 steps, lr 1e-5) on NPO, SimNPO and EvoMU checkpoints of Llama-3-8B-Instruct. It reports the forgetting score over training, which bears on B, on A's 'simple attacks don't recover it', and on F through the EvoMU robustness claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors say, consistent with Fan et al. 2024, that NPO and SimNPO lose forgetting rapidly. EvoMU stays nearly flat for about 800 steps, suggesting stronger resistance, but all methods eventually converge. They interpret this as EvoMU forgetting more thoroughly, an interpretation the eventual convergence weakens.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes EvoMU, an evolutionary search over unlearning losses, and evaluates relearning resistance by fine-tuning on a subset of forgotten WMDP-Bio data; it does not reproduce the original unlearning recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome depends on the unlearning method and the amount of subsequent fine-tuning: EvoMU remains nearly flat for roughly 800 steps, whereas NPO and SimNPO lose forgetting rapidly; all converge after sufficient updates.
record.problems: The relearning result is shown as a figure without exact per-step values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The attack is tested only on WMDP-Bio, with one reported subset size and training setup.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant attack results were omitted. Benchmark-only unlearning scores in Tables 1–4 were left out because they do not measure recovery after an attack.

untested.parts: Only the relearning attack is tested. Prompting, quantization and ablation attacks are not run.
Unrelated or loosely related relearning data, other subset sizes, other learning rates, and other models or benchmarks (only WMDP-Bio on Llama-3-8B-Instruct).
Not tested; quantization is cited only (Zhang et al. 2025).
Not tested on WMDP. TOFU extraction strength uses paraphrased prompts, but this is a standard benchmark metric, not a recovery attack on the unlearned model.
EvoMU is tested against relearning only, under one setup. It is not tested against prompting, quantization or activation ablation.

missing.what: Pre-attack forgetting (1−AccBio) and MMLU for NPO (0.73/0.51), SimNPO (0.75/0.44) and EvoMU (0.75/0.53), plus the original model (0.27/0.65). These serve as baselines for the relearning rows.
Final forgetting level after 1000 relearning steps for each method, which is needed to judge whether recovery reaches the original 0.27.

record.verdict_notes: The relearning experiment is a minor part of a loss-search paper. There is one setup, no seeds or uncertainty, and the curve is figure-only. The y-axis spans 0.25–0.75, so convergence may approach original-model accuracy, but this cannot be confirmed from the text. The authors' interpretation of more thorough forgetting should be weighed against the eventual convergence.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not directly test the full combination of near-chance targeted accuracy, preserved general ability, and resistance to simple attacks.
Tests fine-tuning on 20% of the WMDP-Bio forget set for 1000 steps; does not test unrelated or loosely related examples, other subset sizes, or other relearning datasets.
Activation-direction ablation and whether unlearning blocks access rather than deletes knowledge are not tested.
Prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information are not tested.
Tests EvoMU against the stated WMDP-Bio relearning attack only, not against ablation, quantization, or prompting attacks.
